title: Tolerance Fit Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics
description: Set a designed hole size, a printer size error and a mating part size, and see whether the printed hole is too tight, snug, a good sliding fit or loose. Then predict the outcome for six cases before it is shown. Used in Chapter 7.

educational.topic: Dimensional tolerance and clearance in 3D-printed parts
learningObjectives: Infer whether a printed hole is too tight, snug, a good sliding fit, or loose from its designed size, the printer's size error and the size of the part that goes into it, in six cases, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict the outcome from the numbers and commit, then see the picture and the clearance confirm or correct it
keyQuestions: How much smaller does the hole print than it was designed?
What is the clearance, and which of the four zones is it in?
commonMisconceptions: A hole prints at exactly the size that was designed
A bigger hole is always safer
Zero clearance is a perfect fit
assessmentOpportunities: Six committed outcomes, one attempt each; 5 of 6 for mastery

controls.label: Too tight / Snug / Good sliding fit / Loose
